source.title: Gauss-Newton Unlearning for the LLM Era
source.authors: Lev McKinney; Anvith Thudi; Juhan Bae; Tara Rezaei; Nicolas Papernot; Sheila A. McIlraith; Roger B. Grosse

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether fine-tuning can restore behavior after unlearning, using its own unlearning method and benchmark setup. This is a conceptual test of recovery by fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites earlier work on fine-tuning attacks, but those cited results are not rows. It reports no tests of activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery. It describes K-FADE's intended operation and benchmark results; those are recorded where they bear on version A.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes Zephyr-7b-β models unlearned with K-FADE, RMU and ELM for 200 steps on Wikitext, WMDP Bio retain and a forget subset, then measures WMDP Bio recovery (Sec. IV-D, Fig. 5). This bears on B and on the 'simple attacks don't recover it' part of A. Table I bears on A's suppression and retention parts. K-FADE's authors explicitly do not claim fine-tuning resistance, so F is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say none of the tested methods, theirs or prior ones, resists fine-tuning, so K-FADE does not defend open-weight models. Re-applying the stored update after fine-tuning recovers some unlearning, and works better with K-FADE than with baselines. Their main claim is better specificity at matched suppression, and state-of-the-art results on TOFU.
record.recipe_differences: K-FADE is a new Gauss-Newton/K-FAC unlearning method, not a reproduction of the listed original methods. Its durability experiment fine-tunes unlearned Zephyr-7b-β models for 200 steps on the specified datasets and separately tests transferring the unlearning update.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning dataset affects recovery: K-FADE is most resistant to Wikitext but remains susceptible to related retain-set and forget-set data.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the stored unlearning update back after fine-tuning re-lowers WMDP Bio accuracy, even after forget-set fine-tuning. This works better for K-FADE than for RMU/ELM updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning updates can be transferred via task arithmetic to re-establish unlearning after fine-tuning, when the provider controls the weights.

record.peer_reviewed: 2026 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML); paper says accepted for publication
record.problems: The fine-tuning recovery outcomes in Figure 5 are not given as extractable numbers in the text. The paper does not state WMDP chance accuracy. The attack evaluation is limited to Zephyr-7b-β and the three listed fine-tuning datasets.

untested.parts: Attacks other than full-rank fine-tuning (prompting, quantization, activation edits) were not tested; only Zephyr-7b-β was used.
Only one model, one learning rate and 200 steps. No sweep of relearning-set size, and no WMDP Cyber recovery.
Entire version: no direction ablation or analysis of blocking vs deletion.
Entire version: no prompting, jailbreak or multilingual test.
Entire version: K-FADE is not presented as a robust method, and no robust counter-method is tested.

missing.what: Numeric WMDP Bio accuracies after each fine-tuning attack, including the original-model control and the 25% random line
Transferred-update results for RMU and ELM (described as working worse than K-FADE); no rows recorded

record.verdict_notes: The record wrongly says chance is unstated: Fig. 5 shows 'Random (25%)'. F was mislinked, since the paper explicitly disclaims fine-tuning resistance. RMU comes from an original source (WMDP), but this study is not one. TOFU results concern approximate retraining and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Chance level is not stated, so the paper does not establish whether the unlearned WMDP accuracy is near chance. It tests fine-tuning recovery, but not recovery by internal edits, quantization, or prompting.
The paper tests fine-tuning on Wikitext, WMDP Bio retain data, and a subset of WMDP Bio forget data, not other unrelated or loosely related datasets or other unlearning methods from the claim.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information recovery test.
The robustness experiment concerns full-rank fine-tuning on the specified datasets only; it does not test internal edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.

tranche.reason: K-FADE is a new method aimed at the same question. The fine-tuning experiment tests recovery for K-FADE and for the RMU/ELM baselines.

source_check.notes: Table I values all match. Fine-tuning results (r20-r28) are figure-only; the text gives only 'nearly all' and 'most resistance'. RMU/ELM are the authors' released Zephyr-7b-β checkpoints. The r5-r10 notes saying chance is not stated are outdated: Fig. 5 gives 25%. The paper makes no claim of fine-tuning resistance.

statements.problem: Gives no numbers for this study. Cited r12 (RMU, Zephyr-7b-β, MMLU 58.4 to 57.5) matches. The study's WMDP values for the authors' released RMU checkpoint (Bio 30.4, Cyber 27.1) fit 'near chance'.
Gives no numbers for this study. Cited r23 and r26 match: the text says Wikitext fine-tuning restores RMU and ELM to original WMDP Bio scores (figure-only).

statements.correction: K-FADE, Zephyr-7b-β, 200 steps on Wikitext: shows the most resistance of the methods tested; recovery size is figure-only. Fig. 5 caption: like past methods, K-FADE is not resistant to full-rank fine-tuning. RMU and ELM on Wikitext are restored to original WMDP Bio.
statements.problem: Lists K-FADE on Wikitext (r20) as no or weak recovery under a challenges label. The text only says K-FADE shows 'the most resistance', a relative statement; how much recovers is figure-only. The study's own verdict here is limits_scope.

Matches. Wikitext restores baseline models (RMU, ELM) to original WMDP Bio; overall 'nearly all' returns after 200 steps (AdamW, lr 1e-5, batch 8). Values are figure-only. ELM is the authors' released checkpoint.

Says nothing about this study, though it cites r23. r23 (RMU, Zephyr-7b-β, Wikitext, restored to original) would belong under near-full recovery and conflicts directly with 2501.19202's Zephyr-7B-β Wikitext result.
